question: From 2027, Barco will relocate more than half of its production of surgical and diagnostic monitors from its Saronno (VA) site to China: 71 people will lose their jobs.

Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1197, which implements the International Procurement Instrument (Regulation (EU) 2022/1031), excludes operators originating in China from participating in public procurement procedures for medical devices (CPV33100000-1 to 33199000-1, including monitors, and CPV33195100-4) with an estimated value of at least EUR 5 million and restricts the share of devices originating in China to 50 %.

Below that threshold, or in procurement procedures with other CPV codes, a European firm can provide hospitals with unlimited Chinese devices: unlike the Utilities Directive (2014/25/EU, Article 85), the Public Procurement Directive (2014/24/EU) does not regulate the origin of products. In view of the above: 1.
Does the Commission intend to propose a lower threshold for medical devices, amending the International Procurement Instrument and extending the measure to other CPV codes?
Will it support in the new public procurement regulation (COM(2026)590) a mandatory European preference over products originating in China in procurement procedures for medical devices?
Will it propose, for critical medical devices, a framework similar to that adopted for critical medicines with a view to protecting the Union’s strategic autonomy in the medical sector?
